% =============================================================================
\section{The Idea}
% =============================================================================

% ── Slide 3 — The Idea ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{The Idea — Why LabBank?}

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.50\textwidth}
      \textbf{The ALM challenge}

      A bank's balance sheet produces thousands of cash flows every day.
      Regulatory metrics — NII, EVE, LCR, NSFR — must all be derived
      from those cash flows in a consistent, auditable, reproducible way.

      \vspace{6pt}
      In practice this is complex: rates reset, balances prepay,
      deposits decay, and shock scenarios need to be applied simultaneously
      across every position in every currency.

      \vspace{6pt}
      \textbf{Most systems hide this complexity.}
      LabBank makes it explicit.

      \vspace{8pt}
      \begin{exampleblock}{Core principle}
        Every number in every report traces back to a \textbf{single SQL
        row} in a \textbf{single cash flow table}.
        No aggregation happens before it is recorded.
      \end{exampleblock}

    \column{0.46\textwidth}
      \textbf{What LabBank demonstrates}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item How to build a \textit{complete} ALM pipeline from scratch —
              from raw transaction generation to regulatory submission.
        \item How NII, EVE, LCR, and NSFR are all
              \textit{derived from the same set of cash flows},
              just aggregated differently.
        \item How an IRS overlay shifts the repricing gap without
              touching the balance sheet at all.
        \item How Dagster orchestration enforces dependency order
              and provides an audit log of every pipeline run.
      \end{itemize}

      \vspace{8pt}
      \begin{alertblock}{Scope note}
        \small Balance sheet \textbf{optimisation} (constrained NIM vs
        ΔEVE frontier) is the planned next phase — tensors are pre-built
        but the solver is not yet implemented.
      \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\section{System Architecture}
% =============================================================================

% ── Slide 4 — Architecture diagram ───────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{System Architecture}

  \imgfull[0.97\textwidth]{labbank_architecture.png}

  \vspace{-4pt}
  \small
  \textbf{Four layers:}
  Excel inputs \(\rightarrow\) Python modules (Dagster) \(\rightarrow\) SQL Server (9 schemas) \(\rightarrow\) reports.
  SQL is the single integration bus — every step is independently re-runnable.

\end{frame}

% ── Slide 5 — Pipeline Data Flow ─────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Pipeline Data Flow — Step by Step}

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.48\textwidth}
      \small
      \begin{enumerate}
        \item[\textbf{1.}] \textbf{Balance sheet generation}\\
          Synthetic transactions are drawn from \texttt{bank\_data.xlsx}
          using truncated-normal balance distributions and real historical
          WIBOR rates.
          Written to \texttt{dbo.transactions} and five
          \texttt{schemat.*} child tables.

        \vspace{4pt}
        \item[\textbf{2.}] \textbf{Market data enrichment}\\
          Yield curves bootstrapped and stored in \texttt{mkt.curves}.
          Historical fixings from \texttt{fixing\_input.xlsx} → \texttt{mkt.fixings}.
          Behavioural model parameters (CPR, NMD decay) loaded into \texttt{bs.*}.

        \vspace{4pt}
        \item[\textbf{3.}] \textbf{Cash flow generation}\\
          For every transaction, a full CF schedule is produced:
          contractual amortisation + behavioural adjustments
          (prepayment, deposit decay).
          Written to \texttt{cf.products}.
          Repricing gaps written to \texttt{irrbb.ir\_gap\_*}.

        \vspace{4pt}
        \item[\textbf{4.}] \textbf{IR derivatives (optional)}\\
          IRS legs read from \texttt{irs\_input.xlsx},
          CF schedules written to \texttt{cf.ir\_swap\_*},
          and the swap gap is merged into \texttt{irrbb.ir\_gap\_beh}.
      \end{enumerate}

    \column{0.48\textwidth}
      \small
      \begin{enumerate}
        \item[\textbf{5.}] \textbf{IRRBB calculation}\\
          Six EBA/RTS/2022/10 shock scenarios
          (parallel, steepener, flattener, short-rate)
          applied to all curves.
          NII computed over a 1-year horizon using the repricing gap.
          EVE computed as present value of all run-off cash flows.
          Both written to \texttt{irrbb.*}.

        \vspace{4pt}
        \item[\textbf{6.}] \textbf{Liquidity calculation}\\
          LCR: HQLA vs stressed net outflows over 30 days.\\
          NSFR: available vs required stable funding over 1 year.
          Written to \texttt{results.lcr\_nsfr}.

        \vspace{4pt}
        \item[\textbf{7.}] \textbf{Reporting}\\
          Jupyter notebooks read live from SQL and export
          to HTML and PDF.
          Power BI connects directly to \texttt{schemat.*}
          for interactive repricing gap exploration.
          Excel outputs for IRRBB and LCR/NSFR.
      \end{enumerate}

      \vspace{6pt}
      \begin{block}{Key property}
        \small Steps 5, 6, and 7 can be re-run independently
        without touching the balance sheet or cash flows —
        enforced by Dagster job definitions.
      \end{block}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ── Slide 6 — Dagster Orchestration ──────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Pipeline Orchestration — Dagster}

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.50\textwidth}
      \textbf{Asset graph} (9 software-defined assets)

      \vspace{4pt}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{ll}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Asset} & \textbf{Writes to} \\
        \midrule
        \texttt{balance\_transactions} & \texttt{dbo.*}, \texttt{schemat.*} \\
        \texttt{balance\_add\_data}    & \texttt{mkt.*}, \texttt{bs.*}, \texttt{sched.*} \\
        \texttt{cash\_flows}           & \texttt{cf.*}, \texttt{irrbb.ir\_gap\_*} \\
        \texttt{ir\_swaps}             & \texttt{cf.ir\_swap\_*}, \texttt{irrbb.ir\_swap\_gap} \\
        \texttt{nii\_results}          & \texttt{irrbb.nii\_*} \\
        \texttt{eve\_results}          & \texttt{irrbb.eve\_results} \\
        \texttt{eba\_sot\_results}     & \texttt{results.irrbb\_report} \\
        \texttt{lcr\_nsfr\_results}    & \texttt{results.lcr\_nsfr} \\
        \texttt{optimize\_prep\_tensors} & \texttt{opt\_prep.*}, \texttt{*.npz} \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

    \column{0.46\textwidth}
      \textbf{Business-case jobs}

      \vspace{4pt}
      \begin{description}[labelwidth=0cm,leftmargin=0.3cm]
        \small
        \item[\texttt{balance\_sheet\_job}]
          BS generation + market data + IRS positions.
        \item[\texttt{full\_run\_job}]
          Complete pipeline: BS → CFs → IRS → IRRBB + LCR/NSFR.
        \item[\texttt{irs\_update\_job}]
          Reload swaps → recompute IRRBB only.
          Balance sheet unchanged.
        \item[\texttt{irrbb\_recalc\_job}]
          Recompute NII / EVE / SOT from existing CFs.
          Use after a manual curve update.
        \item[\texttt{liq\_only\_job}]
          Standalone LCR / NSFR refresh.
        \item[\texttt{optimize\_prep\_job}]
          Rebuild fast-metric tensors \& accuracy check.
      \end{description}

      \vspace{4pt}
      \small
      Each asset calls the existing workflow script via subprocess
      — business logic is unchanged, Dagster adds dependency
      enforcement, retry, and a live web UI.
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% =============================================================================
\section{Balance Sheet}
% =============================================================================

% ── Slide 8 — BS Construction ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Balance Sheet Construction}

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.48\textwidth}
      \textbf{Inputs}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item \texttt{bank\_data.xlsx} — product definitions, target
              balances, contractual rates, repricing frequencies, equity.
        \item \texttt{fixing\_input.xlsx} — historical WIBOR / EURIBOR
              fixing time-series used to set variable-rate coupons.
        \item \texttt{dep\_beh\_models\_ir/liq.xlsx} — NMD decay curves
              by product and tenor.
      \end{itemize}

      \vspace{6pt}
      \textbf{How balances are generated}\\
      For each product, individual transaction amounts are drawn from a
      \textbf{truncated normal distribution} anchored to the target balance.
      Maturity dates are sampled from a \textbf{weighted date grid}.

      \vspace{6pt}
      \textbf{How rates are assigned}\\
      Variable/admin products: \(r_{\text{client}} =
        a \cdot \max(r_{\text{index}},\,\text{floor}) + b/100\)
      where $r_{\text{index}}$ is taken from \textbf{real historical WIBOR}
      (not randomly generated).

    \column{0.48\textwidth}
      \textbf{Output tables}

      \begin{exampleblock}{\texttt{dbo.transactions}}
        Master register — one row per individual transaction.\\
        Key cols: \texttt{transaction\_id},
        \texttt{product\_code}, \texttt{bs\_side},
        \texttt{balance\_amt}, \texttt{currency}.
      \end{exampleblock}

      \begin{exampleblock}{\texttt{schemat.*} child tables}
        \texttt{loans} · \texttt{deposits} ·
        \texttt{financial\_instruments} · \texttt{equity} ·
        \texttt{ir\_swaps}\\[2pt]
        Linked via \texttt{transaction\_id}.
        Hold per-transaction rate info (\texttt{rate\_type},
        \texttt{client\_rt}, \texttt{index\_rt}, \texttt{margin}),
        maturity dates, repricing flags,
        and regulatory weights (HQLA, LCR, RSF, ASF).
      \end{exampleblock}

      \vspace{4pt}
      \textbf{Rate types:}
      \textbf{F}ixed (locked) \;|\;
      \textbf{V}ariable (WIBOR + spread) \;|\;
      \textbf{A}dmin (floored at 0\%, policy-set).
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% =============================================================================
\section{Cash Flows}
% =============================================================================

% ── Slide 11 — CF Engine ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Cash Flow Engine}

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.50\textwidth}
      \textbf{What the CF engine does}

      For each product on the balance sheet it generates a full schedule of:
      \begin{enumerate}
        \item \textbf{Capital cash flows} — contractual amortisation plus
              behavioural adjustments (early repayments, deposit decay).
        \item \textbf{Interest cash flows} — coupon payments at the
              contracted client rate, separately tracked per payment period.
      \end{enumerate}

      \vspace{6pt}
      \textbf{Behavioural modelling}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item \textit{Loans:} constant prepayment rate (CPR) applied monthly
              to the outstanding balance.
        \item \textit{Non-maturity deposits (NMD):} exponential decay
              model — a fraction leaves each month; the remainder is treated
              as sticky long-term funding.
        \item \textit{Admin-rate floor:} interest on current accounts is
              capped at 0\% and never passes through to the client as
              a negative rate.
      \end{itemize}

    \column{0.46\textwidth}
      \textbf{Output: \texttt{cf.products}}

      One row per (transaction, payment date). Key columns:

      \vspace{4pt}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{ll}
        \toprule
        Column & Meaning \\
        \midrule
        \texttt{schedule\_id}      & Links to \texttt{schemat.*} \\
        \texttt{cf\_start\_dt}     & Period start date \\
        \texttt{cf\_end\_dt}       & Period end / payment date \\
        \texttt{fwd\_rt}           & Market forward rate \\
        \texttt{client\_rt}        & All-in contracted rate \\
        \texttt{con\_outstanding}  & Contractual balance \\
        \texttt{beh\_outstanding}  & Behavioural balance \\
        \texttt{beh\_capital\_pmt} & Behavioural principal CF \\
        \texttt{beh\_interest\_pmt}& Behavioural interest CF \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

      \vspace{6pt}
      \normalsize
      NII metrics (\texttt{nii\_interest}, \texttt{nii\_renewal}) are
      computed subsequently and stored in \texttt{irrbb.nii\_base\_scenario}.
      EVE uses the full \texttt{beh\_capital\_pmt} run-off schedule.
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% =============================================================================
\section{Repricing Gap \& IR Derivatives}
% =============================================================================

% ── Slide 12 — Repricing gap ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Repricing Gap and Interest Rate Swaps}

  \imgfull{repricing_gap.png}

  \small\vspace{2pt}
  \textbf{Repricing gap} = net volume of assets minus liabilities repricing
  in each tenor bucket.
  A \pos{positive} gap means more assets reprice — the bank \textit{benefits}
  from rising rates in that bucket.
  A \neg{negative} gap signals liability-sensitive exposure.

  \vspace{4pt}
  \textbf{IRS overlay:} swaps shift the gap without touching the balance sheet.
  The swap gap from \texttt{irrbb.ir\_swap\_gap\_beh} is merged into
  \texttt{irrbb.ir\_gap\_beh} before IRRBB calculation.
\end{frame}

% ── Slide 13 — EBA Shock Scenarios ───────────────────────────────────────────

  \imgfull[0.82\textwidth]{shock_curves.png}

  \vspace{-2pt}
  \small
  \textbf{Six supervisory scenarios} are applied to each currency curve;
  shocks are floored at 0\% per tenor.
  PLN shock parameters: parallel $\pm$250 bps,
  short-rate $\pm$350 bps, long-rate $\pm$150 bps.
  The \textit{own} scenario adds a $-$100 bps parallel shock.
\end{frame}

% ── Slide 14 — NII Results ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{IRRBB — NII Results by Scenario}

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.52\textwidth}
      \textbf{NII decomposition}

      \vspace{4pt}
      \small
      NII has two components for each scenario:
      \begin{itemize}
        \item \textbf{Locked interest} — income from CFs already contracted
              (rate and notional fixed). This part is \textit{immune} to
              rate shocks.
        \item \textbf{Renewal} — income from maturing capital reinvested
              at market rates within the 1-year horizon.
              This part \textit{reprices with the curve}.
      \end{itemize}

      \vspace{6pt}
      \normalsize
      \textbf{Result summary} (\texttt{irrbb.nii\_results})

      \vspace{4pt}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{lrrr}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Scenario} & \textbf{NII} & \textbf{\(\Delta\)NII} & \textbf{\(\Delta\)NII/T\textsubscript{1}} \\
        \midrule
        Base           & \multicolumn{3}{c}{\textit{(see ALM\_report.html)}} \\
        Parallel up    & & \pos{+} & \pos{+} \\
        Parallel down  & & \neg{--} & \neg{--} \\
        Steepener      & & & \\
        Flattener      & & & \\
        Short rate up  & & \pos{+} & \pos{+} \\
        Short rate dn  & & \neg{--} & \neg{--} \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

    \column{0.44\textwidth}
      \textbf{NII metric chain}

      \vspace{4pt}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{ll}
        \toprule
        Table & Role \\
        \midrule
        \texttt{cf.products}           & CF schedule source \\
        \texttt{irrbb.ir\_gap\_beh}    & Repricing gap \\
        \texttt{mkt.curves}            & Forward rates \\
        \texttt{irrbb.nii\_base\_scenario} & Per-product NII \\
        \texttt{irrbb.nii\_results}    & Aggregated by scenario \\
        \texttt{results.irrbb\_report} & SOT summary \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

      \vspace{8pt}
      \normalsize
      \begin{block}{Asset-sensitive position}
        \small More assets than liabilities reprice in the short end.
        Parallel-up shocks are \pos{favourable} for NII.
        Parallel-down shocks are \neg{unfavourable}.
        Full numeric results in \texttt{irrbb\_report.xlsx}.
      \end{block}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ── Slide 15 — EVE Results ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{IRRBB — EVE Results by Scenario}

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.48\textwidth}
      \textbf{EVE definition}

      EVE is the present value of all future cash flows under a
      run-off assumption — no new business, existing book winds down
      to maturity:
      \[
        \mathrm{EVE} = \sum_{i} \mathrm{CF}_i^{\mathrm{beh}} \cdot d(t_i)
      \]
      Under a shocked curve $s$, the discount factors change:
      \[
        \Delta\mathrm{EVE}_s = \mathrm{EVE}_s - \mathrm{EVE}_{\text{base}}
      \]

      \vspace{6pt}
      \textbf{Implementation notes}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item EVE loads \textit{all} maturities (no 1-year cut-off),
              making it slower than NII.
        \item Shocked curves are stored in
              \texttt{irrbb.shocked\_curves} and applied
              per-CF at discount-factor level.
        \item A \neg{negative} ΔEVE means the bank's economic net worth
              falls — long fixed-rate assets lose value faster than
              liabilities.
      \end{itemize}

    \column{0.48\textwidth}
      \textbf{Result summary} (\texttt{irrbb.eve\_results})

      \vspace{4pt}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{lrr}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Scenario} & \textbf{\(\Delta\)EVE} & \textbf{\(\Delta\)EVE/T\textsubscript{1}} \\
        \midrule
        Parallel up    & \neg{--} & \neg{--} \\
        Parallel down  & \pos{+}  & \pos{+}  \\
        Steepener      & \neg{--} & \neg{--} \\
        Flattener      & \pos{+}  & \pos{+}  \\
        Short rate up  & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textit{(see irrbb\_report.xlsx)}} \\
        Short rate dn  & & \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

      \vspace{6pt}
      \normalsize
      \begin{alertblock}{Typical long-asset profile}
        \small Fixed-rate mortgages and securities dominate the asset
        side.  Rising rates \neg{reduce} EVE (long fixed assets lose
        value); falling rates \pos{increase} it.
        This creates a natural NII vs EVE trade-off.
      \end{alertblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ── Slide 16 — EBA SOT ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Supervisory Outlier Test (EBA SOT)}

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.48\textwidth}
      \textbf{Methodology}

      The SOT applies a \textbf{50\% haircut} to a scenario's
      $\Delta$EVE if it comes out as a \textit{gain}, before it counts
      toward the regulatory total:
      \[
        \Delta\mathrm{EVE}^{\mathrm{reg}} =
          \min\!\bigl(\Delta\mathrm{EVE},\;0\bigr)
          + 0.5 \cdot \max\!\bigl(\Delta\mathrm{EVE},\;0\bigr)
      \]

      \vspace{6pt}
      \textbf{Thresholds (EBA/RTS/2022/10)}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item EVE SOT: \(\Delta\mathrm{EVE}^{\mathrm{reg}} / T_1 < -15\%\)
              \(\Rightarrow\) \neg{BREACH}
        \item NII SOT: \(\Delta\mathrm{NII}^{\mathrm{reg}} / T_1 < -5\%\)
              \(\Rightarrow\) \neg{BREACH}
      \end{itemize}

      Results written to \texttt{results.irrbb\_report}
      and exported to \texttt{irrbb\_report.xlsx}.

    \column{0.48\textwidth}
      \textbf{SOT result structure} (\texttt{results.irrbb\_report})

      \vspace{4pt}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{ll}
        \toprule
        Column & Description \\
        \midrule
        \texttt{scenario}       & EBA scenario name \\
        \texttt{currency}       & PLN / EUR / USD \\
        \texttt{delta\_eve}     & Raw ΔEVE \\
        \texttt{delta\_eve\_reg}& Regulatory ΔEVE (haircut) \\
        \texttt{sot\_eve\_pct}  & Raw ΔEVE / T\textsubscript{1} \\
        \texttt{sot\_eve\_pct\_reg} & Regulatory EVE / T\textsubscript{1} \\
        \texttt{delta\_nii}     & Raw ΔNII \\
        \texttt{delta\_nii\_reg}& Regulatory ΔNII (haircut) \\
        \texttt{sot\_nii\_pct}  & Raw ΔNII / T\textsubscript{1} \\
        \texttt{sot\_nii\_pct\_reg} & Regulatory NII / T\textsubscript{1} \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

      \vspace{6pt}
      \normalsize
      \begin{block}{Note on the NII SOT haircut}
        \small The 50\% haircut on NII gains (applied at tenor bucket level)
        results in a more conservative SOT ratio than a simple
        total-level haircut — consistent with the regulatory intent.
      \end{block}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% =============================================================================
\section{Liquidity Risk}
% =============================================================================

% ── Slide 17 — LCR / NSFR Results ────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Liquidity Results — LCR \& NSFR}

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.46\textwidth}
      \textbf{Metrics}
      \[
        \mathrm{LCR} = \frac{\mathrm{HQLA}}{\text{Net outflows}_{30\mathrm{d}}} \geq 100\%
      \]
      \[
        \mathrm{NSFR} = \frac{\mathrm{ASF}}{\mathrm{RSF}} \geq 100\%
      \]

      \vspace{4pt}
      \small
      \textbf{HQLA} = Level~1 liquid assets
      (cash, central bank reserves, sovereign bonds)
      at their respective haircuts.

      \textbf{Net outflows} = stressed deposit run-off and
      interbank maturities within 30~days.

      \textbf{ASF} = stable funding weighted by tenor and type
      (equity \& long-term debt score highest).

      \textbf{RSF} = assets weighted by illiquidity
      (loans and illiquid instruments score highest).

    \column{0.50\textwidth}
      \textbf{Result table} (\texttt{results.lcr\_nsfr})

      \vspace{4pt}
      \small
      \begin{tabular}{lrr}
        \toprule
        \textbf{Column} & \textbf{Description} & \textbf{Unit} \\
        \midrule
        \texttt{currency}     & PLN / EUR / USD     & — \\
        \texttt{hqla}         & High-quality liquid assets & PLN m \\
        \texttt{net\_outflow} & Stressed net outflows 30d  & PLN m \\
        \texttt{lcr}          & LCR ratio             & \% \\
        \texttt{asf}          & Available stable funding   & PLN m \\
        \texttt{rsf}          & Required stable funding    & PLN m \\
        \texttt{nsfr}         & NSFR ratio            & \% \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

      \vspace{6pt}
      \normalsize
      Weights applied from \texttt{schemat.deposits}
      (\texttt{lcr\_weight}, \texttt{asf\_weight}) and
      \texttt{schemat.financial\_instruments}
      (\texttt{hqla\_class}, \texttt{haircut}, \texttt{rsf\_weight}).
      Full results in \texttt{lcr\_nsfr\_report.xlsx}.
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ── Slide 18 — Liquidity Gap ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Behavioural Liquidity Gap}

  \imgfull{liq_gap.png}

  \small\vspace{2pt}
  The liquidity gap shows the net cash position across the full
  tenor ladder up to 60~months, using \textbf{behavioural} cash flows
  (loan prepayments included, NMD decay applied).
  The LabBank app's Gap Analysis tab renders this same view interactively,
  alongside its running cumulative total — a sustained \neg{negative
  cumulative gap} is what identifies the point at which the bank would need
  additional funding, the primary input for contingency funding planning.
\end{frame}

\section{Conclusions \& Roadmap}

% ── Slide 20 — Conclusions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
\begin{frame}{Conclusions \& What Comes Next}

  \begin{columns}[T]
    \column{0.52\textwidth}
      \textbf{What LabBank delivers today}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item Full end-to-end ALM pipeline: raw transactions →
              regulatory metrics — reproducible, SQL-backed,
              auditable at every step.
        \item EBA/RTS/2022/10-compliant IRRBB: correct shock construction,
              per-bucket SOT haircut, multi-currency curves (PLN, EUR, USD).
        \item Behavioural realism: loan prepayment (CPR),
              NMD decay (separate IR and LIQ horizons),
              admin-rate floor — not purely contractual.
        \item NII and EVE computed consistently from the \textit{same}
              cash flow schedules — no reconciliation gap.
        \item Dual reporting: ALM/Compliance view and Finance/CFO view,
              both auto-generated from live SQL data.
        \item Dagster orchestration: six business-case jobs with
              dependency enforcement, retry, and a live web UI.
      \end{itemize}

    \column{0.44\textwidth}
      \textbf{Planned: balance sheet optimisation}

      The \texttt{optimize\_prep} module pre-builds vectorised
      sensitivity tensors, enabling (when the solver is added):
      \begin{itemize}
        \item Portfolio optimisation subject to SOT, LCR, and NSFR
              constraints.
        \item Efficient frontier: NIM vs ΔEVE trade-off.
        \item Hedging strategy evaluation (IRS overlay selection).
      \end{itemize}

      Methods are currently in development.

      \vspace{8pt}
      \begin{exampleblock}{LabBank as an educational tool}
        \small Every formula in this presentation has a direct SQL or
        Python equivalent in the codebase.
        The system is designed to make ALM maths \textit{concrete}:
        equations connected to actual data rows you can query.
      \end{exampleblock}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}
